item.title: 🐉 Using HydraFusion Across Copilot Surfaces
item.description:
Picking a model used to be the last decision you made before pressing Enter. Then Auto model selection took that decision away for everyday work. HydraFusion goes one step further: instead of picking one model, it picks a whole workflow, deciding whether a task needs one model, an escalation to a stronger one, or a draft that other models critique before you see it.

HydraFusion is documented under GitHub’s early-access docs and is currently a research preview. That means no SLA, behaviour that can change, and a clear statement from GitHub that it is not intended for production workloads. It is still very usable for real coding tasks today, as long as you understand how it spends AI credits and where it is (and is not) available.

item.title: Choosing a GitHub Copilot AI Model
item.description:
GitHub Copilot offers models from several providers, and the selection changes over time. A model that appears in one Copilot product or plan may not be available in another. Instead of memorising a ranking that will soon be outdated, choose a model for the work in front of you and check GitHub’s live model comparison when you need current details.

The short answer

If you’re unsure, start with Auto. It chooses from the models available to you, taking task complexity and model availability into account. If you need a specific capability or want to control cost, latency or behaviour more directly, select a model yourself and compare it on your real task.
